newsitem.title: USA: Doctors aid teachers with tobacco divestment drive.
newsitem.headline: Doctors aid teachers with tobacco divestment drive.

text.p: University professors pushing their pension fund to sell off its $1.5 billion in tobacco investments got a boost Tuesday from the American Medical Association and former surgeon general C. Everett Koop.

At a news conference called to support the grass-roots divestment drive started by a handful of Midwestern academic retirees, Koop urged fund managers to "take a new look at the tobacco industry" in light of allegations that the industry knew more about the health hazards of smoking than it has revealed.

"Stop new investment and begin orderly divestment," said Koop, who gets some income himself from the TIAA-CREF (Teacher Insurance Annuity Association-College Retirement Equities Fund), the biggest private pension fund.

The AMA, which this year began pushing for health and life insurance companies to divest, helped arrange the Washington appearance for Koop and the academics calling themselves the Educators for Tobacco-Free Investment by TIAA-CREF.
The 1.43 million TIAA-CREF shareholders are college and university faculty, staff and retirees. Certain nonprofit organisations and research institutes are also included.
The educators said they want divestment because "we are providing well over $1.3 billion of respectable collegiate camouflage for cancer."
The shareholders group released excerpts of correspondence between an insurance newsletter and fund Chairman John Biggs confirming that management opposes the shareholder resolution.
A TIAA-CREF spokeswoman was not immediately available.

TIAA-CREF does offer a "social choice" account option that excludes tobacco, but the anti-tobacco activists said it does not allow the same range of retirement investment options that is offered by other TIAA-CREF accounts.

Such shareholder resolutions generally face an uphill battle against management opposition, partly because many people toss out the ballots with the junk mail, have trouble deciphering the technical wording or just never get around to mailing them in.
The TIAA-CREF initiative is part of a small but growing national movement for tobacco divestment, which is reminiscent of the campaign against South African investments in the late 1970s and 1980s.

Some major universities, including Harvard and Johns Hopkins, have purged their portfolios of tobacco investments. Some pension funds, including the state of Maryland and the New York state teachers, have been disinvesting in tobacco, although they said it was a financial and not a social decision.

"As CREF participants, we object on public health, ethical, and financial grounds to our retirement money being invested in America's sleaziest indusry," said Dr. Eugene Feingold, a retired University of Michigan public health professor, former president of the American Public Health Association and a spokesman for the educators' group.
The shareholder ballots are supposed to go out in early October and the meeting is scheduled for New York City on Nov. 11.
